title: EN 18029 exchange conformance and reference-list tooling for veterinary lab and PIMS/LIMS vendors

problem_severity_frequency.rationale: EN 18029 specifies request/result/acknowledgement files but explicitly excludes the code lists needed for unambiguous exchange, and veterinary PIMS/lab APIs are described as closed, undocumented or fee-gated. The problem is plausible and structurally recurring, but no buyer has been shown to feel it as a budgeted pain and no frequency or cost figure is evidenced, so the archetype-aware missing-why-now cap limits this to 2.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: A conceivable buyer set exists (PIMS/LIMS and laboratory software vendors, and laboratories attesting conformance), but no named buyer, budget line, price point or procurement route is evidenced. The UK diagnostic-laboratories software segment is small (USD 6.35m in 2025). Assumption, not evidence, so this is scored 2 with low confidence.

evidence_strength.rationale: The standard's existence and scope are primary-sourced, but there is no evidence of adoption, implementation demand or budget. The register is thin and all three entries leave the central assumption unresolved, so this is a Plausible-level evidence base only.

distribution.rationale: A named target list exists in principle (VetXML consortium members, LIMS vendors), which suggests a plausible direct route, but no prospect has been contacted or evidenced and no channel test has been run. Plausible-but-no-prospects caps this at 2.

differentiation.rationale: No shipping EN 18029 conformance, test-fixture or reference-list product was found, so the exact seam is not demonstrably occupied; but VetXML publishes free schemas and a hub, adjacent middleware exists (Bitwerx, Covetrus Connect) and the why-now is weak (a standard, not a mandate), so the missing-why-now cap limits differentiation to 2.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: The disconfirming question (will any vendor or lab fund conformance tooling without a mandate?) can be tested cheaply by a desk check of vendor documentation plus a small number of approval-gated interviews, with no money required. Medium confidence because no test has yet been run.

feasibility.rationale: Schema validation, test fixtures and mapping tables are buildable from public standards documentation; the hard part is the maintained reference-list content and vendor access, which is plausible but unproven. Scored 3 with medium confidence.

economics.rationale: No price point, contract or margin is evidenced and the buying population (software vendors and labs) is small with a documented one-off tender at GBP 202,652 and a single offer. Economics are modelled assumptions only, which caps this at 2.

founder_fit.rationale: No founder or team detail was available in this run, so founder fit is unscored rather than asserted.

risk.rationale: No legal or regulatory risk: this is a voluntary technical standard, not a mandate, so there is no compliance liability. The main risks are demand risk (vendors may not pay before a mandate) and content-maintenance burden in the reference lists, which are ordinary commercial risks rather than unacceptable ones.

economic_buyer.note: A buyer set can be named (PIMS/LIMS and laboratory software vendors, and laboratories attesting exchange conformance) but no specific buyer, budget or procurement route is evidenced, so this is an assumption, not a pass.
economic_buyer.resolve_via: Ask five named labs/PIMS vendors (VetXML member list) whether a funded EN 18029/VetXML conformance or reference-list need exists and who owns the budget.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: The problem is structurally recurring (every lab-to-prescriber exchange needs mapping and code lists) but no evidence yet shows it is felt as a budgeted pain; no frequency or cost figure is cited.
painful_frequent_or_budgeted.resolve_via: Document vendor and lab statements about conformance effort/cost in the interviews proposed in experiments/vetlab-en18029-conformance-buyer-wedge/plan.md.

non_paid_distribution.note: A plausible non-paid route exists (the public VetXML member list and standards bodies), but no prospect has been reached or evidenced, so the filter is untested.
non_paid_distribution.resolve_via: Attempt direct approaches to at least five named vendors/labs from the public member list and record reply rates.

defensible_wedge.note: No shipping product demonstrably occupies the exact EN 18029 conformance/reference-list seam (competitor existence is not treated as wedge failure), but the wedge is unproven and the standard is voluntary; the missing-why-now cap keeps differentiation at 2.
defensible_wedge.resolve_via: Desk-check whether any vendor ships EN 18029 conformance or maintained cross-walk tooling, and test whether implementers will pay for it absent a mandate.

no_network_effects_needed.note: A single laboratory and a single PIMS/LIMS vendor derive value from validating a file exchange and using a common reference list pair; value does not require a critical mass of participants.

plausible_margins.note: Software margins could be high if reference-list upkeep is light, but no pricing evidence exists and the buyer population is small, so margins are modelled assumptions only (economics capped at 2).
plausible_margins.resolve_via: Test willingness to pay for a conformance package at a specific price in the proposed interviews and compare against estimated upkeep effort.

acceptable_risk.note: No legal, privacy or platform risk is evident for a voluntary standard, but demand risk is material and unassessed because no buyer has been tested.
acceptable_risk.resolve_via: The proposed buyer-wedge experiment will measure whether demand exists before a mandate, which is the principal risk.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: A cheap, decisive test exists: a desk check of vendor documentation plus a small number of approval-gated interviews, costing zero money and about twelve human-hours, with a pre-fixed decision rule.

not_all_optimistic.note: Viability does not depend on every optimistic assumption being true, but several central assumptions (buyer, budget, adoption) remain unevidenced, so this cannot be a pass.
not_all_optimistic.resolve_via: The proposed experiment tests the central assumption directly; if it fails, the idea is killed.
